AdminAgentCategory.description: A category with the number of Agents it holds.
AdminAgentCategory.title: AdminAgentCategory

AdminApiWorkspaceResult.description:
What a wake or hibernate did to one assistant's workspace.

Only ``assistant_id`` is this surface's own. The rest of the object is the
workspace state
(:meth:`~astrabox.core.service.orchestrator.assistant.assistant_service.AssistantService.wake_workspace`
/ ``hibernate_workspace``), which differs per branch — a wake that found a
ready box reports different facts from one that started a bootstrap — so it
is carried rather than flattened into one shape that would be wrong for
most of them.
AdminApiWorkspaceResult.title: AdminApiWorkspaceResult

AdminAsyncioTasks.description: Task totals, and the first 100 pending tasks themselves.
AdminAsyncioTasks.title: AdminAsyncioTasks

AdminDeletedEnvironment.description: The identity of the preset removed by an administrator.
AdminDeletedEnvironment.title: AdminDeletedEnvironment

AdminEnvironmentModels.description:
Model ids an environment's provider can offer.

Empty when the provider publishes no authoritative catalog; the console
then accepts a free-text model id.
AdminEnvironmentModels.title: AdminEnvironmentModels

AdminErrorsPage.description:
Recent failures, session rows and captured runtime errors together.

``counts`` tallies the returned page by source and severity; ``limit`` is
the clamped limit that produced it, not the one that was asked for.
AdminErrorsPage.title: AdminErrorsPage

AdminEvictResult.description: The session whose cached runtime was dropped from this process.
AdminEvictResult.title: AdminEvictResult

AdminFileDescriptors.description:
Open descriptors against this process's own limit.

Every field is null on a platform that does not publish it; a null is
"unknown", which a caller must not render as 0.
AdminFileDescriptors.title: AdminFileDescriptors

AdminFormSchema.description:
The editable schema an admin form renders.

One grammar, two producers:
:func:`~astrabox.core.service.orchestrator.agent_schema.get_agent_schema`
and
:func:`~astrabox.core.service.orchestrator.environment_schema.get_environment_schema`.
``groups`` and ``fields`` are the form's own vocabulary (key, type, enum,
default, help), which the console reads and this module does not interpret.
AdminFormSchema.title: AdminFormSchema

AdminHistoryImportMessage.description:
One earlier message of a migrated conversation.

``blocks`` use the transcript's content blocks: ``text`` and ``image`` for
a user message; for a reply also ``thinking``, ``tool_use`` and the
``tool_result`` answering a call earlier in the same reply. ``completion``
is required on a reply: ``unknown`` when the source recorded no ending.
AdminHistoryImportMessage.title: AdminHistoryImportMessage

AdminHistoryImportRequest.description: Messages in conversation order; a re-run carries the same ones first.
AdminHistoryImportRequest.title: AdminHistoryImportRequest

AdminHistoryImportResult.description: How many messages this call added, and how many were already imported.
AdminHistoryImportResult.title: AdminHistoryImportResult

AdminKillResult.description:
What an admin kill did to one session's sandbox.

``killed`` is True only for a confirmed destruction — something other than
the delete call itself reported the box gone. ``destruction`` carries the
verdict's own name and ``destruction_detail`` the reason, so an unconfirmed
kill is legible as unconfirmed rather than as a failure or a success.
AdminKillResult.title: AdminKillResult

AdminLogsPage.description:
A tail of one log file on the host answering the request.

``available_files`` is what this host actually has, which is empty when the
deployment logs to stderr; ``log_path`` and ``current_file`` name the file
the tail came from, and ``count`` is the number of lines after filtering.
AdminLogsPage.title: AdminLogsPage

AdminMemory.description: Resident memory, null where the platform does not report it.
AdminMemory.title: AdminMemory

AdminNavigationSummary.description: Collection totals displayed in the management rail.
AdminNavigationSummary.title: AdminNavigationSummary

AdminProcessHealth.description:
A live reading of the process answering the request.

Nothing here is stored: every field is measured when the request arrives,
so two calls a second apart legitimately disagree. ``severity`` is the
server's own verdict over these numbers — a caller renders it rather than
recomputing it, so one deployment's thresholds stay in one place.
AdminProcessHealth.title: AdminProcessHealth

AdminRuntimeRow.description:
One session runtime this process is holding open.

The three flags are null when the runtime does not carry that object at
all, which is a different answer from False.
AdminRuntimeRow.title: AdminRuntimeRow

AdminSandboxDiagnostics.description:
One plain-text diagnostic report about one sandbox.

``text`` carries no schema — it is the backend's prose, transported inside
JSON. ``known_scopes`` is the accepted scope vocabulary, not a list of the
reports this sandbox can produce.
AdminSandboxDiagnostics.title: AdminSandboxDiagnostics

AdminSandboxEgressRule.description: One egress rule as the box's sidecar reports it.
AdminSandboxEgressRule.title: AdminSandboxEgressRule

AdminSandboxIdleAction.description: Which idle actions a backend can carry out, and the installation default.
AdminSandboxIdleAction.title: AdminSandboxIdleAction

AdminSandboxIdleSweep.description:
What one forced run of the idle/expiry sweep did.

``summary`` holds the tick's own counters
(:meth:`~astrabox.core.service.orchestrator.expiration_watcher.ExpirationWatcher.scan_once`);
an empty object means neither sweep found a candidate.
AdminSandboxIdleSweep.title: AdminSandboxIdleSweep

AdminSandboxPage.description: One page of a backend's inventory.
AdminSandboxPage.title: AdminSandboxPage

AdminSandboxPagination.description: The backend's own paging counters, passed through.
AdminSandboxPagination.title: AdminSandboxPagination

AdminSandboxQuota.description: The sandbox quota of every enabled backend.
AdminSandboxQuota.title: AdminSandboxQuota

AdminSandboxQuotaBackend.description: One enabled backend's quota, usage and boxes.
AdminSandboxQuotaBackend.title: AdminSandboxQuotaBackend

AdminSandboxQuotaBox.description: One box of the backend's last inventory, with what it is charged.
AdminSandboxQuotaBox.title: AdminSandboxQuotaBox

AdminSandboxQuotaCeilings.description: A backend's quota ceilings; ``null`` is no ceiling.
AdminSandboxQuotaCeilings.title: AdminSandboxQuotaCeilings

AdminSandboxQuotaReservation.description: Room taken for a box the inventory does not show yet.
AdminSandboxQuotaReservation.title: AdminSandboxQuotaReservation

AdminSandboxQuotaUsage.description: What the backend's boxes and pending creates hold against the quota.
AdminSandboxQuotaUsage.title: AdminSandboxQuotaUsage

AdminSandboxSecurity.description: What one sandbox reports about its own containment.
AdminSandboxSecurity.title: AdminSandboxSecurity

AdminSessionFeedHealth.description: The core notification task's lifecycle, with exception values excluded.
AdminSessionFeedHealth.title: AdminSessionFeedHealth

AdminSessionPage.description: One page of the sessions the caller administers.
AdminSessionPage.title: AdminSessionPage

AdminSessionPagination.description: Paging counters for a session listing, counted at the source.
AdminSessionPagination.title: AdminSessionPagination

AdminSessionTrace.description:
A session's latest messages beside one response's browser parts.

``current_response_ids`` are the responses still running.
``message_limit`` and ``part_limit`` are the clamped limits that produced
this answer; ``truncated_part_count`` is how many earlier parts of the
selected response the limit left out.
AdminSessionTrace.title: AdminSessionTrace

AdminSystemOverview.description:
Process facts plus the session distribution, counted at the source.

``session_state_counts`` and ``total_sessions`` are scoped to the sessions
the caller administers, so they move with who is asking.
AdminSystemOverview.title: AdminSystemOverview

AdminThreads.description: Thread totals, and the first 200 threads themselves.
AdminThreads.title: AdminThreads

AdoptedConnector.description: An app just connected, and the caller's Assistants it was turned on in.
AdoptedConnector.title: AdoptedConnector

AgentAccess.description:
The Agent authorization settings returned by ``_agent_access_view``.

``created_by`` is stamped on insert and is absent from documents seeded
without an owner, so it is the one optional member of the response.
AgentAccess.title: AgentAccess

AgentCategory.description: One Agent category, in the administrator's order (``position``, from 0).
AgentCategory.title: AgentCategory

AgentEnvironmentModels.description: The model ids an Environment's gateway offers. Empty when it offers none.
AgentEnvironmentModels.title: AgentEnvironmentModels

AgentEnvironmentOption.description: One Environment an Agent author may choose, without its secrets.
AgentEnvironmentOption.title: AgentEnvironmentOption

AgentExtensionCatalog.description:
The provider's catalog with this Agent's selection marked.

The selected ids are read back from the stored assignments rather than from
the request, so what the form shows ticked is what Session start resolves.
AgentExtensionCatalog.title: AgentExtensionCatalog

AgentExtensionItem.description:
One selectable catalog entry, as ``ExtensionCatalogItem.public_view``
exposes it. MCP servers and Skills share this shape; ``transport`` is set
on the entries whose provider declares one.
AgentExtensionItem.title: AgentExtensionItem

AgentFormField.description:
One field of the Agent authoring form, as ``agent_schema`` declares it.

``key`` and ``type`` are the two members every entry carries; the optional
presentation and validation members (``group``, ``required``, ``enum``,
``path``, ``complex``, ``advanced``) appear per field. ``item_schema``
describes the sub-fields of a nested object with this same grammar.
``default`` is the value an Agent created without the field has. Two
fields carry one: ``prepared_capacity``, whose value follows the
deployment, and ``artifacts_enabled``, which is on.
AgentFormField.title: AgentFormField

AgentFormGroup.description: One form section. ``id`` is the contract; the label is frontend i18n.
AgentFormGroup.title: AgentFormGroup

AgentFormSchema.description: The editable shape of an Agent, as the console's form editor reads it.
AgentFormSchema.title: AgentFormSchema

AgentListPage.description:
One page of the Agents the caller may see, by name regardless of case.

``next_cursor`` is the value to pass back as ``cursor``; it is ``null`` on
the last page, which ``has_more`` reports independently. ``total`` and
``enabled`` count every Agent the caller may see, whatever ``q`` and
``status`` narrowed, and come with the first page only.
AgentListPage.title: AgentListPage

AgentMCPServerAssignment.description:
The built-in-catalog MCP servers selected for one Agent.

``missing_mcp_server_ids`` names assignments whose server is gone, so the
console can show the gap rather than a silently shorter list.
AgentMCPServerAssignment.title: AgentMCPServerAssignment

AgentPreparedRuntimeStatus.description: Platform-owned capacity waiting for this Agent's next conversation.
AgentPreparedRuntimeStatus.title: AgentPreparedRuntimeStatus

AgentRecord.description:
One stored Agent as these routes project it.

The Agent document is open — ``AgentService._sanitize`` passes through
every key that is not internal — so the fields named here are the ones the
console addresses by name, and ``extra="allow"`` carries the rest. Their
types are the ones ``agent_schema.AGENT_FIELD_SCHEMA`` enforces on write,
plus the identity and ownership fields ``AgentConfigService`` stamps.
``artifacts_enabled`` is always present because a read reports the switch
as it takes effect, including for an Agent stored without it.

``can_manage`` is computed per viewer and therefore present only on the
reads that compute it (list and get), not on a write's echo of the record;
``favorited`` and ``can_start_conversation`` are present on the full list.
The latter reports configured admission eligibility, not runtime health.
AgentRecord.title: AgentRecord

Assistant.description:
One Assistant's catalog row, as ``AssistantService._sanitize_assistant``
renders it.

The row is open — sanitizing removes the storage id and the credential
bindings and passes the rest through — so the members named here are the
ones the console addresses by name and ``extra="allow"`` carries the rest.

``workspace_state`` and ``current_sandbox_id`` are not stored on the row:
list and detail reads join them from the workspace. An Assistant whose
workspace was never built reports ``workspace_state="NOT_MATERIALIZED"``.
Assistant.title: Assistant

AssistantDefaults.description: The layer as stored, with the Environment new Assistants would use now.
AssistantDefaults.title: AssistantDefaults

AssistantDefaultsExtensionCatalog.description: The extension catalog with the deployment layer's selection marked.
AssistantDefaultsExtensionCatalog.title: AssistantDefaultsExtensionCatalog

AssistantDefaultsFields.description: The layer's authored fields, named as an Assistant's own are.
AssistantDefaultsFields.title: AssistantDefaultsFields

AssistantDeletion.description:
Confirmation that an Assistant's catalog row was soft-deleted.

The row is severed only after its sandbox is proven destroyed, so a caller
that receives this knows no box outlived the name. A destruction that
cannot be confirmed refuses with ``ASSISTANT_SANDBOX_UNDESTROYED`` instead,
keeping the Assistant resolvable so the delete stays retryable.
AssistantDeletion.title: AssistantDeletion

AssistantExtensionCatalog.description: The provider's catalog with this Assistant's selection marked, as for an Agent.
AssistantExtensionCatalog.title: AssistantExtensionCatalog

AssistantListPage.description:
One page of the caller's Assistants, the most recently edited first.

``next_cursor`` is the value to pass back as ``cursor``; it is ``null`` on
the last page, which ``has_more`` reports independently. ``total`` and
``ready`` count every Assistant the caller owns, whatever ``q`` and
``status`` narrowed, and come with the first page only.
AssistantListPage.title: AssistantListPage

AssistantScheduledJobs.description:
What an Assistant scheduled for itself, read from its program's own store.

Each job carries the program's own field names (Hermes: ``id``, ``name``,
``prompt``, ``schedule_display``, ``state``, ``next_run_at``,
``last_run_at``, ``last_status``, ...). ``jobs`` is null when there is no
live list to read, and ``reason`` says why: ``workspace_not_running`` or
``engine_keeps_no_schedule``.
AssistantScheduledJobs.title: AssistantScheduledJobs

AssistantWorkspace.description:
An Assistant workspace's posture after a wake.

Waking is a request to reach ``READY``, not a wait for it. ``state`` says
where the workspace is: ``READY`` names ``current_sandbox_id``;
``MATERIALIZING`` names the ``provisioning_session_id`` that is building it,
which the caller polls; ``RECOVERY_REQUIRED`` names the sandbox whose
destruction is unconfirmed, and blocks a rebuild until it is released.
A completed hibernate has no sandbox to resume: wake materializes a fresh
one from the configured workspace medium.
AssistantWorkspace.title: AssistantWorkspace

AssistantWorkspaceDestruction.description:
Confirmation that an Assistant's workspace was destroyed.

The Assistant's catalog row survives; a later wake builds a fresh
workspace for it.
AssistantWorkspaceDestruction.title: AssistantWorkspaceDestruction

AssistantWorkspaceHibernation.description:
The outcome of taking an Assistant workspace offline.

The storage provider carries the files; ``released`` means the old sandbox
was proven gone and a later wake may prepare a fresh one from that medium.
``recovery_required`` retains ``sandbox_id`` when destruction was not
confirmed, so the operation remains retryable without losing the box's
last name.
AssistantWorkspaceHibernation.title: AssistantWorkspaceHibernation

ChannelAccountLinkRecord.description: One participant of a trigger and the AstraBox account its messages run as.
ChannelAccountLinkRecord.title: ChannelAccountLinkRecord

ChildRunMessagePage.description: The engine-owned transcript of one Session child run.
ChildRunMessagePage.title: ChildRunMessagePage

ChildRunRecord.description: One engine-owned child run projected at Session scope.

active.description: The engine reports active work, independently of resource closure.
active.title: Active

tool_call_ids.description: Tool invocations associated with this child by its engine.
tool_call_ids.title: Tool Call Ids

ChildRunRecord.title: ChildRunRecord

ChildRunStopResult.description: Acknowledgement that an engine-owned child run was asked to stop.
ChildRunStopResult.title: ChildRunStopResult

Connector.description: One work app: whether it is set up, and the caller's connection to it.
Connector.title: Connector

ConversationEndResult.description:
The outcome of ending an Assistant conversation.

Supported for Assistant conversations only; an Agent conversation is
refused. The conversation's runtime is disposed, and its history survives.
ConversationEndResult.title: ConversationEndResult

CreateCredentialRequest.description:
Body for ``POST /api/v1/admin/vaults/{vault_id}/credentials``.

``auth`` is the (open) credential document — the vault service validates its
``type`` and shape and splits out the write-only secret fields.
CreateCredentialRequest.title: CreateCredentialRequest

CredentialAllowedRequests.description: Method / path limits on the requests a credential may authenticate.
CredentialAllowedRequests.title: CredentialAllowedRequests

CredentialAuthSummary.description: Key fields and rules of one credential — never a secret payload.
CredentialAuthSummary.title: CredentialAuthSummary

CredentialBinding.description: The Vaults an administrator bound to one Agent or Assistant.
CredentialBinding.title: CredentialBinding

CredentialDelivery.description: How saved values reach a sandbox — mechanisms, never the values.
CredentialDelivery.title: CredentialDelivery

CredentialInjectionLocation.description: Where egress placeholder substitution is allowed; at least one is true.
CredentialInjectionLocation.title: CredentialInjectionLocation

CredentialNetworking.description: Egress policy for one credential; ``allowed_hosts`` only when limited.
CredentialNetworking.title: CredentialNetworking

CredentialRefresh.description: Non-secret half of an OAuth refresh configuration.
CredentialRefresh.title: CredentialRefresh

CurrentUser.description:
The identity the request resolved to, as the console reads it.

The three optional fields are what an identity provider filled in; the
no-auth resolver asserts a user id and roles alone, so they arrive as null
rather than being absent. The obligations that come with declaring a
response model are in :mod:`astrabox.api.routes.response_envelope`.
CurrentUser.title: CurrentUser

DeletedChannelAccountLink.description: The participant whose link is gone; ``deleted`` is false if it had none.
DeletedChannelAccountLink.title: DeletedChannelAccountLink

DeletedDeployment.description: The binding that is gone. ``deleted`` confirms it and its channel records were deleted.
DeletedDeployment.title: DeletedDeployment

DeploymentExtensionProvider.description: The deployment's extension provider; ``provider`` is null when it runs no catalog.
DeploymentExtensionProvider.title: DeploymentExtensionProvider

DeploymentRecord.description:
One trigger binding on an Agent or Assistant, as ``DeploymentService`` stores it.

``secret`` is the credential the calling system signs with, returned so the
configurer can register it there. A record reports the settings its binding
has; ``extra="allow"`` carries the ones a scene adds (``channel_config``,
``schedule``, ``callback_base_url``, ...).
DeploymentRecord.title: DeploymentRecord

DeploymentTriggerAck.description:
What an inbound trigger is told once the work is durable.

A channel provider may merge its own acknowledgement fields into this
answer — a platform echoing back a verification challenge, for instance —
so unlisted members are part of the contract, not an accident.
DeploymentTriggerAck.title: DeploymentTriggerAck

EnsurePrimaryAssistantRequest.description: What a first-created primary Assistant starts with; ignored when it exists.
EnsurePrimaryAssistantRequest.title: EnsurePrimaryAssistantRequest

ExposedPortUrl.description:
A freshly minted browser-reachable URL for one sandbox port.

The URL is short-lived and carries its own bearer, so a caller re-requests
it rather than caching it.
ExposedPortUrl.title: ExposedPortUrl

ExtensionConsoleSession.description:
Where to send the browser, and how long the grant lasts.

The session itself lives in the cookies the route sets; the body carries no
token, so a client that logs or forwards it discloses nothing. The
obligations that come with declaring a response model are in
:mod:`astrabox.api.routes.response_envelope`.
ExtensionConsoleSession.title: ExtensionConsoleSession

ExtensionConsoleSessionRequest.description: Which kind of catalog entry the management console is opened for.
ExtensionConsoleSessionRequest.title: ExtensionConsoleSessionRequest

ExtensionProviderView.description:
The extension provider whose catalog this deployment offers.

``name`` is the ``ASTRABOX_EXTENSION_PROVIDER`` value that selects it;
``display_name`` and ``management_console`` are what the provider declares
(``ExtensionProviderFeatures``).
ExtensionProviderView.title: ExtensionProviderView

HeldInputView.description: An input the platform still holds: accepted, not yet durably taken by the runtime.
HeldInputView.title: HeldInputView

InheritedExtensions.description:
What an Assistant inherits from the layers above it, by name and source.

Credential Vaults are counted, not named; nothing here can be edited
through the Assistant.
InheritedExtensions.title: InheritedExtensions

InputReceipt.description:
An accepted input. Its response arrives on the session's stream.

``duplicate`` is true when the same ``client_message_id`` was accepted
before; the receipt then describes that earlier input, including its
recorded refusal in ``failure`` when it failed.
InputReceipt.title: InputReceipt

InteractionAnswerReceipt.description: An answer stored for the runtime; the response continues on the stream.
InteractionAnswerReceipt.title: InteractionAnswerReceipt

InterruptReceipt.description: ``accepted`` when a reader will pass the interrupt on; ``idle`` when nothing runs.
InterruptReceipt.title: InterruptReceipt

IssuedMCPClientToken.description: The mint's answer — the only place the secret is ever returned.
IssuedMCPClientToken.title: IssuedMCPClientToken

MCPClientToken.description:
One key, as ``mcp_client_token_service.public_view`` renders it.

There is no ``secret`` field: it exists only in the issuing answer below, so
a reader cannot mistake an absent secret for an empty one.
MCPClientToken.title: MCPClientToken

MCPClientTokenList.description: Every key the calling user holds.
MCPClientTokenList.title: MCPClientTokenList

MCPServer.description:
One registered remote MCP server.

``MCPRegistryService._view`` returns the stored document minus its private
keys, so the fields and their order are the document's own.
MCPServer.title: MCPServer

MCPServerList.description: Every MCP server registered in the organization.
MCPServerList.title: MCPServerList

NativeStateInitialization.description: The allocation whose unpublished profile is being recovered.
NativeStateInitialization.title: NativeStateInitialization

PermissionModeUpdate.description:
The outcome of setting a session's permission mode.

``applied`` reports whether the running engine took the new mode, not
whether the request was accepted: a session with no live runtime records
the mode and answers ``false``.
PermissionModeUpdate.title: PermissionModeUpdate

PersonalScheduleCreate.description: The owner and execution identity come only from the authenticated request.
PersonalScheduleCreate.title: PersonalScheduleCreate

ProcessSummaryState.description:
The generated label for one response's folded work.

``status`` is ``generating`` while a writer holds the claim, ``completed``
once the label exists, and ``failed`` when the model call did not produce
one — a failed label can be asked for again with ``retry=true``.
``disabled`` means label generation is switched off, not a failed request.
``response_completed`` distinguishes work that ran to an answer from work
that stopped short.
ProcessSummaryState.title: ProcessSummaryState

ResponseView.description:
A response the runtime produced, as its reader recorded it.

``status`` is ``running``, ``waiting`` or ``ended``; ``outcome`` is
``completed``, ``failed`` or ``cancelled`` once ended, and
``native_reason`` is the engine's own word for the ending, carried
verbatim.
ResponseView.title: ResponseView

RuntimeStateOwnerPayload.description: The platform-issued owner of a native runtime profile.
RuntimeStateOwnerPayload.title: RuntimeStateOwnerPayload

SandboxCallbackResult.description:
The disposition of one control-plane callback.

``handled`` false carries ``ignored`` naming why — a callback for an unknown
session, or one fenced out by a newer sandbox generation. ``handled`` true
carries the subject it applied to and the status it applied. The fields of
the arm that did not run are absent rather than null, so a caller reads the
outcome from which keys are present.
SandboxCallbackResult.title: SandboxCallbackResult

SandboxTerminatingResult.description:
Which Session projections converged, and which were expected to pause.

Agent and Assistant-workspace owners are converged by the same operation but
are not exposed in this in-box compatibility response. A notice is always
``handled``: a box with no owner is normal for unclaimed prepared capacity.
``ignored`` maps a Session id to the planned pause that preserved its box.
SandboxTerminatingResult.title: SandboxTerminatingResult

SandboxTermination.description:
The outcome of reclaiming a session's sandbox.

The conversation survives — history is durable and the next turn rebuilds a
sandbox. ``killed`` distinguishes a sandbox this call destroyed from one
that was already gone.
SandboxTermination.title: SandboxTermination

SessionArchival.description:
Confirmation that a session was archived.

Archiving terminates the sandbox as well, so the fields of
:class:`SandboxTermination` accompany the archive flag.
SessionArchival.title: SessionArchival

SessionChildRunPage.description: All child runs visible in one Session, in tree order.
SessionChildRunPage.title: SessionChildRunPage

SessionDeletion.description: Confirmation that a session was soft-deleted. Deletion is final.
SessionDeletion.title: SessionDeletion

SessionDirectoryCreated.description: The created directory, addressed both as a location and as a target.
SessionDirectoryCreated.title: SessionDirectoryCreated

SessionFileChangeResponse.description: One ended response and every file change it made; empty when it changed none.
SessionFileChangeResponse.title: SessionFileChangeResponse

SessionFileChanges.description:
The responses that ended after ``after_seq``, through ``through_seq``.

``through_seq`` is the next ``after_seq``. Each response replaces what a
reader held for it.
SessionFileChanges.title: SessionFileChanges

SessionFileEntry.description:
One directory member.

``size`` and ``modified_at`` come from the sandbox's directory listing, so
only a listing carries them; the entries an upload echoes back name what was
written and nothing else. Both stay optional here so the upload answer keeps
the same entry shape without inventing a size it never measured.
SessionFileEntry.title: SessionFileEntry

SessionFileListing.description:
A directory read: where the panel is, and what is in it.

``parent_path`` is null at the session root — the panel's "up" control is
that value's presence, not a comparison it re-derives.
SessionFileListing.title: SessionFileListing

SessionFileMoved.description: Source and destination, resolved to absolute paths inside the root.
SessionFileMoved.title: SessionFileMoved

SessionFilePreview.description: An expiring bearer URL for a file and its workspace-relative resources.
SessionFilePreview.title: SessionFilePreview

SessionFileUploadResult.description: What an upload wrote, in the directory it wrote to.
SessionFileUploadResult.title: SessionFileUploadResult

SessionFilesDeleted.description:
The requested paths, and how many of them existed to be removed.

``deleted_count`` is below ``len(paths)`` when a path was already absent:
deletion converges, so a retry after a lost response still answers 200.
SessionFilesDeleted.title: SessionFilesDeleted

SessionHistoryBlockDetails.description:
The parts one folded ``data-process-block`` header stands for.

One message carrying the folded parts in their original order.
``has_more`` is always ``false``: a header's contents are whole, and there
is nothing further to page through.
SessionHistoryBlockDetails.title: SessionHistoryBlockDetails

SessionHistoryBlockPage.description:
One page of the conversation with each ended response's work folded.

The messages of :class:`SessionMessagePage`, where the work of a response
that had ended is replaced by ``data-process-block`` parts that
:class:`SessionHistoryBlockDetails` reopens. ``next_cursor`` is what to send
back as ``before``; it pins every older page to the output position the
first page was read at (``output_seq``).
SessionHistoryBlockPage.title: SessionHistoryBlockPage

SessionListPage.description:
One page of summarized sessions, newest first.

``next_cursor`` is the value to pass back as ``cursor``; it is ``null`` on
the last page, which ``has_more`` reports independently.
SessionListPage.title: SessionListPage

SessionMessagePage.description:
One page of a session's conversation as AI SDK UI messages, oldest first.

A user message is an input the session accepted; an assistant message is
one response, its stored parts folded the way the AI SDK folds them live.
``before`` is the cursor for the next older page. The first page also
carries ``output_seq``, the output position its parts were read through,
to follow the stream from, and the interaction waiting on the owner. A
share link's page carries neither ``output_seq`` nor the tool input of an
interaction.
SessionMessagePage.title: SessionMessagePage

SessionRead.description: When the owner last read a conversation.
SessionRead.title: SessionRead

SessionRecord.description:
One session, as the read paths project it.

The list summarizes each row (``session_runtime/views.py``
``session_summary``): its state there comes from the row's lifecycle and
the runtime status the reader last cached. The detail adds what the
runtime is doing from its recorded facts: the responses in progress, the
last one that ended, the interaction waiting on the owner, the inputs the
platform still holds, and ``output_seq``, the output position to follow the
session's stream from.
SessionRecord.title: SessionRecord

applicable.description: Whether execution prerequisites apply; false for read-only history
applicable.title: Applicable

SetAgentAccessRequest.description: The complete policy accepted by the dedicated Agent access endpoint.
SetAgentAccessRequest.title: SetAgentAccessRequest

SetCredentialBindingRequest.description: Ordered Vault ids selected by an administrator for one runtime.
SetCredentialBindingRequest.title: SetCredentialBindingRequest

ShareLink.description:
The share configuration its owner may read back.

The token is the capability, so it appears here and nowhere the viewer side
answers. ``expires_at`` is null for a link with no expiry — a distinct state
from an expired one, which the viewer routes refuse with 404.
ShareLink.title: ShareLink

ShareRevoked.description:
Revocation answers the one fact it changed.

The token is deliberately absent: revoking disables the link without
discarding the token, so re-sharing keeps links already handed out working,
and there is nothing here for a client to treat as a live capability.
ShareRevoked.title: ShareRevoked

SharedMessagePage.description:
One page of a shared conversation as UI messages, newest page first.

``before`` is the cursor for the next older page. A share has no stream to

SharedSession.description:
A session as a link recipient sees it.

A capability URL grants reading the conversation, not access to the owner's
session or its runtime. Only what the read-only page shows crosses this
boundary: the title, the interaction the conversation waits on (without
the tool input it asks about), and whether files may be downloaded.
SharedSession.title: SharedSession

StartConversationRequest.description:
Conversation start body.

Credentials are deliberately absent. They are bound to the managed Agent or
Assistant configuration; accepting a user-supplied Vault id here would let a
conversation replace that management decision. Keeping an empty, strict
model lets ``POST`` without a body and ``{}`` work while unknown fields fail.
StartConversationRequest.title: StartConversationRequest

Conversation creation answers with the session itself, so the members of a

traffic for it then goes to ``/api/v1/sessions/{session_id}/...``.

TranscriptLoadResult.description:
A scope's entries, or ``None`` for a key nothing has written.

The null is the SessionStore contract for "unknown key" and is distinct from
an empty list, so the adapter can tell a never-written transcript from one
whose entries were all removed.

get.description: Return the authoritative editable schema for the Agent form.
Return the authoritative editable schema for the environment form.
List all environment presets (including disabled entries).

delete.description: Delete a preset only after checking its Agent and Assistant references.

put.description: Upsert a single environment preset by name.

get.description:
Model ids the console can offer for agents on this environment.

Enumerated by the environment's selected model provider. A provider with
no authoritative catalog returns an empty list and the console accepts a
free-text model id.
List management consoles enabled for this deployment.

Which idle actions a backend can carry out, and which one is in force.

The question a form has to ask before offering an environment the choice:
an ``idle_action`` the backend cannot honor is refused at write time, and a
control that offers it anyway makes the operator discover that by being
rejected.

Whether a backend implements pausing is a property of the code, declared
on the seam, so there is nothing to be unreachable and ``supported`` is
a plain boolean.

What it therefore does not answer: whether this cluster is arranged for
snapshots. Pausing additionally needs a containerd at the standard socket,
a CRI that pulls locally, and a registry both the node and a Pod can
reach (docs/providers/opensandbox.md). A backend that declares pausing on
a cluster missing one of those pauses nothing — the commit fails, the box
is left running, and the sweeper says so. So this reports capability, and
the form's copy carries the cluster requirement; neither pretends to be
the other.

``default_action`` is the installation's own setting. It seeds the field
when an environment is created and is not consulted again: a stored
environment always carries its own action, so a sweep reads that and
never this.

post.description:
Run the idle/expiry sweep once, now, and answer with what it did.

The expiration watcher normally invokes this sweep every 300 seconds. This
endpoint invokes the same scan immediately, so checking idle parking or
dead-binding convergence does not add the watcher interval to any cluster
operation.

Read-only in the sense that matters: it takes no arguments and can decide
nothing the timer would not have decided on its next tick. It is a
`POST` because it acts.

The summary is the tick's own — `idle_candidates` / `idle_parked` /
`idle_active` / `idle_failed`, plus the dead-binding counters — so a caller
sees why nothing happened, which is usually the question. An empty object
means neither sweep found a candidate.

get.description:
Each enabled backend's quota ceilings, what is held against them, and its boxes.

Usage is the backend's last inventory plus the reservations for boxes
it does not show yet, as the quota itself counts it; ``inventory_at``
says when that inventory was taken.

One page of the backend's sandbox inventory.

Paged at the source: ``pagination`` carries the backend's own counters,
so the console advances by ``page`` while ``has_next_page`` holds rather
than assuming one response is the whole inventory.
One sandbox as its backend's control plane describes it.

One plain-text diagnostic report, passed through as text.

``text`` is prose for a human to read — no schema, no promised fields,
no stability across backends or backend versions. It is returned inside
the JSON envelope purely as transport; render it verbatim and do not
parse it. ``truncated`` marks a report the provider had to cap.

``***`` in the text is a value the backend withheld, and a run of them
is normal rather than a fault: a backend that cannot prove where a
withheld value ended keeps masking to the end of the report. When a
report reads that way, the later sections are readable as their own
scopes.

A backend or server that does not produce the report answers 501 with
its own reason, so the caller learns the report cannot be had and why,
instead of receiving empty text that reads as a healthy, silent
sandbox.

``known_scopes`` is the scope vocabulary this route accepts
(:data:`~astrabox.seams.sandbox.SANDBOX_DIAGNOSTIC_SCOPES`) — a constant,
and named as the constant it is. It is deliberately not called
"available": support is per backend and, for a control plane fronting
several runtimes, potentially per runtime, so which of these four this
sandbox can actually produce is knowable only by asking for each one.
A field that promised availability would be advertising reports the same
backend goes on to refuse.

What this box reports about its own containment.

Asked of the sandbox, not of the control plane: an operator opening
this panel wants to know whether the egress policy and the credential
vault their deployment configured actually took effect, and an answer
derived from that configuration cannot tell them. So every field is the
box's answer.

``available: false`` is a finding, not a failure. It means no egress
sidecar answered — the box has no egress policy and no vault, whatever
was intended — and it carries the reason. A backend that cannot ask a
box at all says so the same way, which an operator can tell apart from
an uncontained box because the detail names the backend.

Credentials appear by name only. The vault is write-only by
construction; no stored value can be read back, here or anywhere.

Stream every transcript the caller may manage as one gzip tar archive.

Each session uses the SDK's directory layout, so untarring under
``~/.claude/projects/`` makes its transcript resumable. The service applies
owner scope and the requested agent/date filters in the session query.

The route writes and releases one session's files at a time instead of
assembling the complete archive in memory. Sessions without mirrored
transcript entries are omitted.

post.description: Evict cached runtime from memory (simulates request hitting a different machine).

Import a migrated conversation's earlier messages, for reading only.

Nothing runs: no sandbox, command or turn. Import before the conversation's
first message of its own; a session that already has one refuses with
``HISTORY_IMPORT_AFTER_CONVERSATION``. A re-run of the same messages
changes nothing; other content under a used ``source_id``, or a new message
placed before imported ones, is ``HISTORY_IMPORT_CONFLICT``.

get.description:
The session's transcript as the Claude Agent SDK stores it.

A single ``<sdk-session-id>.jsonl`` when the session has only its main
conversation: dropped into any directory under ``~/.claude/projects/``,
``claude --resume <sdk-session-id>`` continues it. A ``.tar.gz`` preserving
the SDK's directory layout when subagent transcripts exist, because those
are separate files and shipping only the main one would silently drop them.

The media type therefore follows the artifact rather than being fixed: the
two cases are different files, and answering `.jsonl` for a session with
subagents would either misname the archive or drop the subagent
transcripts.
Secret-free Environment choices for the Agent form.
Searchable model ids exposed by the chosen Environment's gateway.
Agent form structure for any signed-in Agent author.

get.description:
Return a fresh browser-reachable URL for a sandbox port.

The request itself is authenticated and ownership-checked before the
platform mints a new short-lived bearer URL.

The success answer is the envelope dict, not a ``JSONResponse`` holding
it: FastAPI sends a response object through untouched, which would
leave ``response_model`` describing this route without checking it.
What the console offers for extension catalogs; reads no catalog.

post.description:
The box says it is going away. The platform decides who that affects.

Scoped to the box, not to a conversation, because the box is what knows
and a box can have Session, Agent, and Assistant-workspace owners. It
reports one fact — "I am being torn down" — and the platform resolves
every durable owner by ``sandbox_id``. The box asserts none of those
relationships; they are platform state.

A Pod also exits during an intentional lifecycle transition. The owner
records that intent before touching the box, so the convergence
operation preserves:

* a parked Session and its Agent-owned shared-box pointer;
* an Assistant workspace whose files committed and whose old box is
  being released, plus every Session attached to it;
* a Session already being ended or deleted.

A notice from a box with no durable owner is not an error — it is normal
for a box whose owners moved on and for unclaimed prepared capacity.

get.description:
Read the conversation with each ended response's work folded away.

``before`` is a ``next_cursor`` from an earlier page; omitting it starts at
the newest entries and pins the output position every later page reuses.

Reopen one folded ``data-process-block`` and return the parts it replaced.

``cursor`` is the one the header carried, and is required: it pins the read
to the output position of the page that folded the parts.

post.description: Accept a message for the conversation.

Write, or return, the label for one response's folded work.

Answers with the stored label when there already is one. ``retry=true``
asks again for a label whose generation failed; a completed one is returned
unchanged.

get.description:
The session's output after ``after_seq``, then live, through the end of one response.

Each part is an AI SDK UI message chunk; ``data-resume-cursor`` parts carry
the position to reconnect from.

post.description: Stop the command the session's terminal runs; answers once the command has ended.

get.description:
Follow a terminal command again: its recorded events after ``after_seq``, then live.

The stream ends with the command's ``exit``; each event carries its
``seq``. Without ``command_id`` it follows the command the terminal runs
now and answers ``204`` when none runs.

post.description:
Run one command in the session's terminal and stream its events as SSE.

The events are ``ack`` (carrying the ``command_id``), ``stdout``,
``stderr``, ``cwd`` and a final ``exit``. The command runs on when the
stream closes; ``GET`` on this path follows it again. WebSocket is
intentionally avoided; the terminal uses HTTP SSE.

get.description:
Liveness endpoint.

Returns a static ``ok`` payload. Intentionally dependency-free (it does
not touch the database, Docker daemon, or any provider) so it answers even
before the runtime is wired — it reports that the HTTP server is up, which
is exactly what the container HEALTHCHECK and load balancers need.

Liveness stays ``ok`` through a drain (see ``/readyz``): a draining
replica must not be killed by a liveness probe before it finishes its
in-flight turns.

Readiness endpoint for rolling deploys.

200 when this replica should receive new traffic; 503 during shutdown
or after its core notification listener ends unexpectedly. In-flight
turns are not killed by this probe. See ``astrabox/api/readiness.py``.
